status: Open - closes 5:00pm AEDT 31 January 2027
best_for: State, territory or council-led construction that addresses road safety, productivity, bridge renewal, flood and disaster resilience, road sustainability or heavy-vehicle rest areas. It is not a direct community grant or a technology-development fund.
funding: Up to $5 million per eligible project; $200 million per year is the program envelope, not an applicant amount. Every project requires a funding co-contribution.
deadline: Tranche 6 opened 1 September 2026 and closes 5:00pm AEDT 31 January 2027 (4:00pm AEST in Brisbane).
applicants: Australian state or territory governments and local government authorities only. A community group, business or technology developer cannot lead the application.

name: Screen Australia Future Leaders Delegation - BitSummit 2027
status: Open - closes 5:00pm AEST 5 November 2026
best_for: Early-to-mid career Australian gamemakers who have already released a game publicly and have another game ready to present at BitSummit 2027. It does not fund an unreleased simulator or an early game idea.
funding: $6,000 per successful delegate towards flights, accommodation, event tickets, ground transport and meals; travel to the required Melbourne pre-departure workshop is covered separately.
deadline: Applications close 5:00pm AEST Thursday 5 November 2026.
applicants: Eligible Australian citizens or permanent residents, or eligible Australian incorporated companies nominating a delegate, with an active ABN, any required GST registration, rights to present the project, at least one publicly released game and a current game ready for public presentation.

name: Screen Australia Narrative Content Production - December 2026
status: Open - closes 5:00pm AEST 3 December 2026
best_for: Production-ready Australian narrative content for online or direct-to-audience release, television or theatrical feature film, with an experienced team, rights, viable budget, audience pathway and compliant marketplace finance.
funding: Varies by project scale, primary platform, production budget and additional finance under the current program guidelines; no single applicant cap is published on the official program page.
deadline: Applications close 5:00pm AEST Thursday 3 December 2026. Applicants must discuss the project with a Screen Australia Investment Manager before applying.
applicants: Eligible Australian production applicants and production-ready projects meeting Screen Australia Terms of Trade, program guidelines, team, rights, budget, audience, marketplace and finance requirements. First Nations participation or content has additional requirements.

name: Community Broadcasting Foundation Quick Response Grants
status: Rolling - eligible emergencies and genuinely time-limited opportunities may be considered outside ordinary rounds
best_for: Eligible community media organisations facing an unforeseen threat to transmission or operations, or a genuinely time-limited opportunity that could not have been anticipated for the last round and cannot wait for the next one. It is not routine capital funding for a planned LED screen.
funding: Varies by evidenced need; eligible emergencies may receive up to 100% of project cost, while eligible time-limited opportunities may receive up to 50%. No fixed applicant cap is published.
deadline: Rolling discussion and invitation pathway. Eligible proposals are considered outside normal rounds, with the official page stating applicants normally receive an outcome within one week.
applicants: Eligible community media organisations able to evidence an unforeseen emergency or time-limited opportunity, inability to wait for the next round, lack of reserves or insurance coverage, technical need, quotes, budget and organisational financial information.

name: National Regional Roads Australia Mobile Program
status: Future - expected to open in the third quarter of 2026; final guidelines and dates are not yet published
best_for: Future multi-carrier mobile coverage on eligible regional and remote highways and major roads. Treat this as a connectivity and resilience source watch only until the final guidelines confirm eligible applicants, locations, project readiness and funding amounts.
funding: $30 million is the national program envelope; the amount available to an applicant is TO BE CONFIRMED in the final guidelines
deadline: The official page says the national program is expected to open in the third quarter of 2026. No opening or closing date is published as at 26 September 2026.
applicants: TO BE CONFIRMED in the final guidelines. The draft consultation described registered applicants with shovel-ready projects, but that is not a final eligibility decision.

name: Queensland SES Support Grant 2027-28
status: Opening soon - the official page says the 2027-28 round will open in early October 2026
best_for: Future council-led facilities, vehicles and other resource support for recognised SES groups or units. This is not a general community resilience grant and requires an invited local government applicant plus confirmed SES need and authority.
funding: TO BE CONFIRMED for the 2027-28 round. The official page states the previous 2026-27 round offered up to $150,000 for facility projects and up to $75,000 for vehicle projects; those caps must not be assumed for the new round.
deadline: Expected to open in early October 2026. The official page does not yet publish a closing date for the 2027-28 round.
applicants: Invited Queensland local governments applying to support recognised SES groups or units; final 2027-28 eligibility, scope and evidence requirements remain TO BE CONFIRMED.
